how1Body: Submit a research question or a short text document.

f2Body: Each claim is labelled supported, disputed, or unverified.

evBody: Every report separates what the evidence says from the AI's own synthesis, and says where it is unsure.
evSupported: Several credible sources agree and none contradict the claim.
evDisputed: Credible sources disagree, or the evidence points in different directions.
evUnverified: Not enough reliable evidence was found to judge the claim.
evNote: These labels are the AI's assessment, not proof. Source links and dates may be wrong, so open them before you cite them.
uc1Body: Get a structured starting point and sources to read next.
uc2Body: Scan a topic's claims and debates before a deeper review.
uc3Body: Sort claims into supported, disputed, and unverified.
uc4Body: Draft market and competitor overviews quickly.
uc5Body: Prepare client briefs with clear limitations.
uc6Body: Give teams a consistent report format.
freeFeature: 3 reports per month · All research modes · Copy, Markdown, and PDF export
proFeature: 15 reports per month · All research modes · Copy, Markdown, and PDF export · Email support
enterpriseFeature: Custom report volume · API access · Tailored onboarding
payNote: Paid plans are not self-serve yet. Contact us to sign up. Free limits reset on the 1st of each month.
priv1: Your question, any attached text, and your options are sent to an AI provider to write the report.
priv2: Verfiai does not save your questions or reports on its servers. Reports stay in your browser until you close or refresh the page.
priv3: Don't include personal or confidential information. There are no accounts yet, and your free-report count is stored only in your browser.
a1: The AI breaks your topic into individual claims, compares what it knows from different sources, and labels each claim supported, disputed, or unverified. It is an aid to checking, not a guarantee.
a2: From the AI model's training knowledge. Verfiai does not search the live web, so links can be outdated or wrong. Open every source before relying on it.
q3: How long does a report take?
a3: Usually 20 to 60 seconds, depending on the topic and mode.
q4: Which languages and files are supported?
a4: Reports can be written in 19 languages. You can attach .txt or .md files up to 200 KB.
q5: How many reports can I create?
a5: 3 free reports per month, counted in your browser. Pro Researcher includes 15 per month.
a6: Yes. Copy the text, download it as Markdown, or use Print to save it as a PDF.

howIngestBody: Paste text, a link, a reference list or a question. Speak it if you prefer.
howExtractBody: Verfiai splits text into individual claims or references and searches the web and Crossref for each.
howEvaluateBody: Two AI engines weigh the evidence independently; disagreements go to a third. Every verdict links to its sources.
howLimitations: Limitations: Verfiai can't read paywalled sources, can miss recent events, and AI engines can misread evidence. Treat results as a starting point and open the sources.
useCasesTitle: Built for research that needs an audit trail
researchersBody: Validate citations and investigate the evidence behind claims before submission.

trustDetail: Verfiai extracts claims and gathers relevant publicly available evidence, recording source links, excerpts and retrieval times. Two AI engines assess each claim, with a tie-break when they disagree. Outputs are decision support, not definitive truth judgments. Search coverage may be incomplete due to paywalls, indexing limits or recent publication dates.
cardClaimBody: Paste a statement, article or draft. Verfiai identifies factual claims and shows evidence that supports, contradicts or needs further review.
cardReportBody: Ask a question and receive a structured, cited research report with key findings, source links, excerpts and limitations.
cardCitationBody: Review references for metadata issues, retractions, missing details and other citation risks.
trustPoint1: Verfiai searches available sources and evaluates the evidence for each claim.
trustPoint2: Results are labelled Supported, Contradicted, Mixed evidence or Insufficient evidence.
trustPoint3: Confidence reflects the available evidence: source quality, diversity, recency and consistency of assessment.
trustPoint4: AI agreement is one signal, not proof that a claim is definitively true.
trustPoint5: Open the sources, review the context, and apply your own judgment for important decisions.
